title: Sunny Sunflower: log your time in the sun and grow a sunflower
description: Head outside and your sun time adds up on its own, then use it to grow your own sunflower. Free, and your history stays on your device.

hero.headline:
Grow a sunflower
with today's sunshine
hero.lead: Step outside and your sun time adds up by itself. Give the sunlight you collect to your sunflower to keep it thriving. Forget it for a few days and it starts to wilt.
hero.cta: Get it free on the App Store
hero.note: Every feature is free. Your history stays on your device.

problem.title: How many minutes of sun did you actually get today?
problem.text: A few steps on the way to work, a quick lunch run. Spend the day indoors and you only realize in the evening that you barely saw daylight. Sunny Sunflower puts your outdoor time into numbers, and your sunflower is there waiting for tomorrow's walk.

features.title: It measures on its own once you're out
features.text:
Tap `Go get some sun` and head outside. The app reads the brightness around you from the front camera's exposure data. Once the light stays outdoor-bright for about 30 seconds, tracking begins. No photos are ever taken or saved.
After that, the sensor wakes for just 20 seconds every 2 minutes to save battery.

features.title: Keep a daily log of sun and mood
features.text: In the calendar, each day gets its sun time, a mood emoji and a short note. Spent time outside without tracking it? Use `Add outdoor time` to add anywhere from 5 to 120 minutes.

features.title: See your week and month at a glance
features.text:
Weekly and monthly stats show the days you hit your goal and your average sun time. Set a daily goal from 10 to 120 minutes and see right on the home screen how many more minutes you need today.
Widgets on the Home Screen and Lock Screen, plus the Dynamic Island, show today's sun and how your sunflower is doing.

items.title: Set a daily goal
items.text: It starts at 30 minutes. Change it anywhere from 10 to 120 in Settings.

items.title: Head out into the sun
items.text: Tap `Go get some sun` and keep the app open as you step outside. It asks for camera access once.

items.title: Feed your sunflower
items.text: Tap `Give to sunflower` to turn the sunlight you collected into energy.

reference.title: How light turns into sunlight
rows: Dim light: doesn't count as sun time
minutes × average lux ÷ 3,000 (up to 100% per session)
drops 2.5% an hour, about 60% a day
reference.note: You can set the outdoor threshold anywhere from 100 to 2,000 lux in Settings. The default is 300 lux.

items.a: It estimates the brightness around you from the front camera's exposure data. When the light stays outdoor-bright for a short while, tracking starts by itself. No photos are taken or saved.
Once sunlight is confirmed, the sensor doesn't stay on. It wakes for about 20 seconds every 2 minutes to re-check, and a simple timer covers the rest.
Your sunflower loses 2.5% of its energy every hour. Collect some sun, then tap `Give to sunflower`. On a clear day, 15 to 20 minutes in direct sun is enough to make up for a full day.

items.q: I was outside but nothing was logged.
items.a: Use `Add outdoor time` at the bottom of the home screen to add 5 to 120 minutes. If tracking struggles to start on cloudy days, lower the outdoor threshold in Settings.

items.q: How does the friends feature work?
items.a: When you and a friend are close (within about 10 m) and both tracking sunlight, you connect automatically. Someone new has to confirm sharing the sun first; after that it's automatic. Your petals turn colorful and fade back over 3 days, and your time together is saved in the Friends tab. Both of you need the app, plus Bluetooth and Local Network access.
Yes. No ads, no purchases, every feature included. If you like it you can leave a tip in the app, but tipping doesn't unlock anything extra.

items.q: Can I back up or move my history?
items.a: Everything stays on your device with no server involved, and the last 90 days are kept. There's no separate export, but your history is included in your regular iCloud or computer backup.

items.q: How do I delete all my data?
items.a: Go to Settings > Data > `Reset data` in the app, or delete the app. This can't be undone.

items.q: Where do I report a bug?
items.a: Email us at the address below or open an issue at github.com/M1zz/SunlightTracker/issues. Your device model, iOS version and what happened help a lot. We usually reply within a few days.
